To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a pre-operative AB word score of ≤15% was found to be a reasonable criterion for predicting post-operative performance for adult CI candidates.
a pre-implant AB word score of <15% is a reasonable predictor of a good post-implant performance in adults with acquired sensorineural hearing loss.
we have developed a new criterion for CI candidacy based on the AB word test, and that this criterion is now being used as part of the All Wales National Cochlear Implant Audit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a pre-operative assessment of the likelihood of a successful outcome from cochlear implantation.
the use of a pre-operative AB word score of < 15% as an indicator that a patient has a reasonable chance of achieving post-operative improvement with a CI.
the use of a mono-syllabic word score to determine whether a candidate for a CI has a reasonable chance of post-operative improvement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
an AB word test score of 15–20% is a reasonable pre-implantation assessment criterion for CI candidacy for adult candidates with acquired hearing loss.
a 15% pre-implant AB word score is a useful predictor of post-implant performance for adult CI patients.

a score of 15%, on the pre-operative AB word test, is a criterion that is associated with a reasonable chance of post-operative improvement in adults with acquired severe to profound hearing loss, and should be considered as part of the CI candidacy process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a 15% mono-syllabic word score on AB word testing is a reasonable predictor of a successful outcome following cochlear implantation in adults with a ski-sloping hearing loss and should be considered as part of the assessment criteria for cochlear implantation.
an AB word test of 15% or less is a reasonable predictor of post-implant performance.
a pre-operative AB words score of 15%, in a patient with a ski-slop hearing loss, would be a reasonable indication for cochlear implantation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the AB words test can be used to identify patients who are likely to have a reasonable chance for post-implantation benefit.
it is possible to use existing post-operative data to establish a new pre-operative criterion for implantation in adults.
it is possible to establish a pre-operative assessment score that predicts post-operative performance in CI users.
